rulings.challenge_claim: The row's forward seam (10:14|10:15) carries the chapter's strongest undisclosed Hebrew continuity signal, while the disclosed hazard (the WEB continuation-paragraph fold) is tier-4 English-rendering metadata with no Hebrew correlate.
rulings.grounds: Independently re-derived: a skeleton-tier adjacency sweep over MT ch10 (content tokens, len>=2, stoplist-filtered) returns exactly 3 shared-token adjacent pairs -- (10:12,10:13), (10:14,10:15), (10:16,10:17) -- matching eccl_device_inventory's sentence_zone_texture count for ch10 (3 of 19) exactly. 10:14 carries לֹא יֵדַ֤ע (oshb:Eccl.10.14, byte) and 10:15 carries לֹֽא יָדַ֖ע (oshb:Eccl.10.15, byte) -- the negated root joined at the forward seam. P03-017's own boundary_rationale and device_notes name only the WEB fold and reject only the backward (10:12-13) alternative; the forward root-echo goes unmentioned in this row. The fold itself is real (2 book-wide sites, WEB 7:8/10:14, tier-4 per the toolkit) and correctly navigated for quotation purposes, but it is English-rendering metadata, not a pointed-text signal -- so the row's stated confidence basis and its actual strongest cross-seam signal point in different directions. Does not change the unit_type call: single_saying is still correct (a shared root without a shared construction does not meet the cluster bar), and the disclosure gap is closed from the other side in P03-018's device_notes.
rulings.remedy: Add one sentence to P03-017's device_notes disclosing the negated-root echo with the following verse (byte: לֹא יֵדַ֤ע / לֹֽא יָדַ֖ע) as thematic-only cross-seam texture, mirroring the disclosure already carried in P03-018 from the other direction. Symmetry fix only; single_saying stands.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's rejected_alternative states the two verses share 'no shared construction,' which is byte-false since both carry a negated qal of the root ידע.
rulings.grounds: Byte-confirmed: לֹא יֵדַ֤ע (oshb:Eccl.10.14, prefix/imperfect conjugation) and לֹֽא יָדַ֖ע (oshb:Eccl.10.15, suffix/perfect conjugation) -- same root, negated, different conjugations. Independently re-swept the contiguous two-word skeleton phrase 'lo-yada/yeda': returns exactly 6 verses book-wide (MT 4:13, 6:5, 8:5, 9:12, 10:14, 10:15), with 10:14/10:15 the only adjacent pair -- matches the challenge's cited sweep exactly. But the row's own device_notes already state 'the not-knowing motif shared with the preceding verse is named as thematic texture' -- so the underlying byte fact is disclosed elsewhere in the same row. The rejected_alternative's phrase 'no shared construction' is imprecise but defensible as shorthand distinguishing a bare shared root (different conjugations, no repeated formula) from a true repeated construct/phrase (the kind bridging 10:16-17). Per the owner-ruled sentence-zone bar (a cluster whose only glue is a shared theme is over-clustering), a shared root without a shared construction does not license a cluster, so the underlying single_saying call is policy-correct independent of this wording. This is a precision defect in the rejected_alternative's phrasing, not a boundary defect -- refine, not the flat 'byte-false' the challenge claims.
rulings.remedy: Re-cut the rejected_alternative to name the shared root explicitly and distinguish it from a repeated construction, e.g.: '...rejected because, although both verses negate the root ידע (לֹא יֵדַ֤ע / לֹֽא יָדַ֖ע, different conjugations, no repeated construct phrase), the two verses address distinct topics with no shared construction.' Sharpens the existing disclosure; does not reverse it.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the melekh_sites citation ('royal vocabulary shared with the chapter-closing verse') names an inventory object whose 9-member list excludes both 10:16 and 10:17. OL converges on the same miscitation and additionally argues the repeated 'land, whose king' phrase is mislabeled a construct phrase, and that the true cohesion (4 shared content tokens) is stronger than the row discloses.
rulings.grounds: Independently re-derived against eccl_device_inventory.json's frame_seams.melekh_sites object: refs = [1.1, 1.12, 2.12, 4.14, 5.8, 8.2, 8.4, 9.14, 10.20] (count 9, count_object = tokens with article/prefix forms of מלך) -- confirmed neither 10.16 nor 10.17 is a member, matching both primaries exactly. A further independent contiguous-skeleton sweep of bare מלך book-wide returns 11 verses, likewise excluding 10.16/10.17, reproducing LF's own re-sweep. The shared element אֶ֔רֶץ שֶׁמַּלְכֵּ֖ךְ / אֶ֔רֶץ שֶׁמַּלְכֵּ֖ךְ is a relative-particle-plus-2fs-suffixed noun, structurally outside that object's defined article/prefix scope -- the final-letter-allography/suffix-escape class the shared hazard catalog names. On OL's added grammar point: independently confirmed the first word carries a disjunctive accent (zaqef qaton) in both verses and is followed by the relative-plus-suffixed-noun, not a second absolute or construct noun; a suffixed noun cannot serve as nomen rectum in a construct chain, so 'land, whose king' is address (vocative) plus a relative clause, matching the row's own English gloss, not a genitive/construct chain. On the under-citation point: independently re-derived the token overlap between 10:16 and 10:17 as {ארץ, שמלכך, ושריך, יאכלו} -- confirmed 4 shared content tokens by direct byte comparison (וְשָׂרַ֖יִךְ בַּבֹּ֥קֶר יֹאכֵֽלוּ / וְשָׂרַ֨יִךְ֙ בָּעֵ֣ת יֹאכֵ֔לוּ), matching OL's count and confirming this is the single strongest of the 3 shared-token adjacent pairs in ch10. LF's and OL's melekh_sites points are the SAME defect (convergent); OL's construct-phrase and under-citation points are DISTINCT additional findings LF did not raise. None of this threatens the saying_cluster call -- if anything the cohesion is stronger than claimed.
rulings.remedy: (1) Drop or correct the 'melekh_sites' citation in observed_substrate_signals -- either omit it or disclose that the suffixed royal-noun form falls outside that object's article/prefix scope. (2) Replace 'construct phrase' in boundary_rationale with an accurate label (e.g. a repeated address-plus-relative-clause formula). (3) Optionally strengthen the rationale by naming all 4 shared content tokens rather than only the opening phrase. saying_cluster call stands.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's 'opens with the imperative clause' claim and its 'doubled imperative' label both hold only in English word order/translation; in the Hebrew the curse clause is not verse-initial and the negated form is not a true imperative.
rulings.grounds: Independently confirmed against oshb:Eccl.10.20 (byte): the verse's actual first two words are גַּ֣ם בְּמַדָּֽעֲךָ֗ ('even/also in your thought'), with מֶ֚לֶךְ אַל תְּקַלֵּ֔ל beginning only at the third word -- the row's 'opens with' claim reflects WEB's reordered rendering ('Don't curse the king, no, not in your thoughts'), not the Hebrew's own word order. Independently confirmed the grammar point: the verb in מֶ֚לֶךְ אַל תְּקַלֵּ֔ל and in אַל תְּקַלֵּ֖ל carries a taw preformative (prefix/imperfect conjugation, 2ms), and Biblical Hebrew negates commands with אל plus the prefix conjugation, never with a true imperative; the contrast is demonstrable inside this same cluster's own bytes -- שַׁלַּ֥ח לַחְמְךָ֖ (oshb:Eccl.11.1), תֶּן חֵ֥לֶק (oshb:Eccl.11.2), and זְרַ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6) are genuine imperatives (no preformative), while אַל תַּנַּ֣ח (oshb:Eccl.11.6) is the same negated-prefix-conjugation pattern as the two 10:20 occurrences. The doubling itself (the two-word negated sequence occurring twice in the verse) is correctly reported. On the row's third, weaker ground (unit_type resting on 'one grammatical sentence'): that argument is form-based (sentence-completeness), consistent with how neighboring rows (10:18, 10:19) argue sentence-hood, not pure tier-4 verse-count metadata as characterized -- and 10:20 is the terminal verse of the owner-ruled second sentence zone (9:17-10:20) where single_saying is the operative default independent of this argument's strength. That sub-point is not upheld as framed; the positional and grammatical-labeling defects are.
rulings.remedy: Correct boundary_rationale: (a) do not describe the curse clause as verse-opening -- name גַּ֣ם בְּמַדָּֽעֲךָ֗ as the verse's actual opening words, with the curse clauses following; (b) relabel 'imperative clause'/'doubled imperative' as a negated prefix-conjugation (jussive-pattern) form used for negative commands, not a true imperative -- a form claim argued from the pointed bytes per the toolkit's standard (no machine morphology layer exists to auto-check this). unit_type (single_saying) stands, independently grounded in the sentence-zone default.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the row's only rejected_alternative addresses splitting v.1 from v.2, never the real rival of uniting 11:1-6 into one admonition_unit, which the book strategy itself names as the candidate span; the negated-knowledge refrain this row introduces continues through 11:5-11:6. OL: the forward seam (11:2|11:3) carries an undisclosed byte-true repeated phrase 'al ha'aretz,' one of only 2 content-token-sharing adjacent pairs in all of ch11.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed against the row's own text: strongest_rejected_alternative reads 'Reading v.1 alone as a single_saying, separate from v.2, is rejected because...' -- addresses only the v.1/v.2 split, never a merger with 11:3-6. The governing book strategy explicitly names 'imperative counsel units (e.g. 11:1-6 candidates)' as the admonition_unit candidate span -- so the unaddressed rival is the strategy's own named candidate, not a primary-invented alternative. Independently re-derived the negated-knowledge distribution: the two-word negated form closing 11:2 recurs at 11:5 (לֹ֤א תֵדַע֙, byte), and the negated-existential-plus-participle form (אֵֽינְךָ֤ יוֹדֵ֨עַ֙, byte) recurs at 11:6 (אֵֽינְךָ֨ יוֹדֵ֜ע, byte) -- confirming a real cross-seam epistemic recurrence beyond this row's own span. On OL's forward-seam point: independently re-swept the contiguous phrase 'al ha'aretz' book-wide -- 7 verses (MT 5:1, 8:14, 8:16, 10:7, 11:2, 11:3, 12:7), with 11:2/11:3 the only adjacent pair among them (byte-confirmed: עַל הָאָֽרֶץ closing 11:2; עַל הָאָ֣רֶץ opening the clause at 11:3) -- and independently confirmed via token-overlap that this is 1 of only 2 catchword-adjacent pairs in all of MT ch11 (matches eccl_device_inventory's count exactly: 2 of 9), the other being 11:5/11:6. Independently confirmed the back seam (10:20|11:1) carries zero shared content tokens, so OL's claim that 11:1-2's imperative pairing is well-founded on the back side stands. LF's and OL's items converge on the same underlying defect (the real 11:1-6-unification rival is undisclosed/unaddressed), argued from two complementary byte signals -- the epistemic refrain forward from v.2, and the הָאָֽרֶץ phrase forward from v.2 into v.3 -- not a duplicate finding.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite strongest_rejected_alternative to engage the real rival: state and rebut (from bytes) why 11:1-2 stands as its own admonition_unit rather than folding into one 11:1-6 span, addressing both the negated-knowledge refrain's continuation into 11:5-11:6 and the repeated phrase at 11:2/11:3. This is a boundary-adjacent proposal: if no byte-grounded rebuttal survives, P03-023 and P03-024 should be considered for merger into one 11:1-6 admonition_unit row -- a boundary change requiring explicit boss adoption, not made here.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the row's rejected_alternative is a strawman on the same 11:1-6-unification question as P03-023. OL, more extensively: the stated cohesion binder (negated-knowledge clause) covers only 2 of the span's 4 verses and its first member is conceded to be row-external at 11:2 without rebuttal; the imperative/jussive-frame bounds required by the owner ruling are never actually derived (only 11:6 carries one); and the cited reut_ruach/rayon_ruach wind-vocabulary signal is device-inventory-absent from the row's own span and from all of ch11.
rulings.grounds: Independently confirmed all four sub-claims. (1) Distribution: the two-word negated form (לֹ֤א תֵדַע֙, byte) occurs at 11:2 and 11:5 only; the negated-existential-plus-participle form (אֵֽינְךָ֤ יוֹדֵ֨עַ֙ / אֵֽינְךָ֨ יוֹדֵ֜ע, byte) occurs at 11:5 and 11:6 only -- absent from 11:3 (cloud/tree conditional) and 11:4 (wind-observer participle clause) -- confirmed by direct verse inspection, matching OL's '2 verses each' sweep exactly; covers 2 of the row's 4 verses, not all 4. (2) The row's own boundary_rationale states the refrain 'is introduced one verse earlier at the row-external verse Eccl.11.2 (its own admonition_unit), which this unit continues without restating' -- confirmed this concession is present verbatim, and confirmed no rebuttal follows explaining why that continuation does not argue for unity with 11:1-2 -- the same gap LF names from the P03-023 side. (3) Imperative/jussive-frame derivation: independently confirmed the span's only imperative is זְרַ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, byte), paired with the negated jussive-pattern אַל תַּנַּ֣ח (oshb:Eccl.11.6, byte); 11:3 opens on a conditional (אִם), and 11:4 turns on a participle plus לֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ע (negated prefix-conjugation, not a 2nd-person directive) -- so three of the row's four verses carry no directive form, and the strategy-mandated 'argued from the imperative/jussive frames' derivation is not actually performed in the row. (4) Independently confirmed against eccl_device_inventory.json's reut_ruach object (7 refs: 1.14, 2.11, 2.17, 2.26, 4.4, 4.6, 6.9) and rayon_ruach object (2 refs: 1.17, 4.16) -- neither list contains any ch11 verse; the row's own span carries only bare ruach forms, שֹׁמֵ֥ר ר֖וּחַ (oshb:Eccl.11.4, byte) and דֶּ֣רֶךְ הָר֔וּחַ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, byte), the literal sense (observing/way of the wind), not the idiomatic vanity formula -- confirming this citation names a device object that is byte-absent from the row's own span, the resh-ayin-family conflation the shared hazard catalog specifically warns against. Additionally independently verified two positive byte signals OL flagged as available but uncited: the cloud lexeme (contiguous substring עבים) occurs at exactly 3 verses book-wide (Eccl.11.3, Eccl.11.4, Eccl.12.2 -- byte-confirmed הֶעָבִ֥ים / בֶעָבִ֖ים / הֶעָבִ֖ים), and the sowing root's two attested forms (זְרַ֣ע at 11:6; יִזְרָ֑ע at 11:4) each occur at exactly the 2 verses OL names, confirmed as token-distinct forms that would escape a naive token-equality adjacency check. LF's and OL's items converge on the strawman-rejected_alternative point (same defect as P03-023, argued from this row's side); OL's other three sub-findings (uneven refrain coverage, missing imperative-frame derivation, reut_ruach/rayon_ruach miscitation) are additional, distinct, and independently confirmed.
rulings.remedy: (1) Correct or remove the reut_ruach/rayon_ruach citation from observed_substrate_signals; if a wind-vocabulary signal is wanted, cite the any-ruach object (20 verses, book-wide) accurately and name the literal, non-idiomatic sense used here. (2) Either derive the admonition_unit bounds from an actual imperative/jussive-frame argument that accounts for 11:3-11:4's non-directive forms, or reconsider the span. (3) Rewrite strongest_rejected_alternative to engage and rebut the 11:1-6-unification rival (paired with the P03-023 remedy) rather than only the internal v.5-doubling question -- same boundary-adjacent proposal as P03-023: if the rebuttal doesn't survive, propose merging P03-023+P03-024 into one 11:1-6 admonition_unit row for boss adoption.
